notes: SEED / DRAFT — hand-authored on 2026-09-17 to create the repository; reduced to the listing only on 2026-09-26.
This file is the LISTING: one row per template repository we keep, website and app alike.
It is a human index, NOT the machine source of truth. Every template is its own repository,
ever-works/<name>-template, and that repository holds the template's spec (.works/works.yml),
its shape (.works/template.yml) and its documentation (README.md). Nothing here copies them.
The platform discovers templates by scanning catalogOrganization for repositories whose name ends
in 'template' and reads each one's own files. This file adds curation (pin, license class,
managed-hosting decision, verification) and makes a template listed, badgeable and searchable.
Status 'placeholder' = not released yet: the repository may exist, but no release tag v<blueprint.version> exists, so template.sha is null and nothing has been verified on a cluster.

`template.ref` is a branch for a website row (the existing fork-from-branch behaviour) and for an app row while it is a placeholder; on release an app row's `template.ref` becomes the tag `v<blueprint.version>` and `template.sha` that tag's commit (see CONTRIBUTING.md).
THIS IS THE e2e BRANCH: main plus test-only rows for the App Works acceptance lanes (APW-13 T29). dev/stage pin EVER_WORKS_APPS_CATALOG_REF to a commit here; production never reads this branch.

CI (tools/validate-specs.mjs) validates this file against schema/templates-manifest.schema.json and, for every app row, fetches .works/works.yml from the row's repository at template.sha or template.ref and validates it against schema/app-spec.schema.json.

templates.name: Cal (community build)
templates.summary: Open-source scheduling: booking pages, calendar sync, reminders and a large Next.js app.

managedHosting.reason: Upstream recommends personal, non-production use; the community build stays on the user's own cluster.

trademark.notice: Cal.diy® is a trademark of Cal.com, Inc. This community build is not affiliated with or endorsed by Cal.com, Inc.

notes: Template repository ever-works/cal-template (renamed from ever-works/cal-diy-template; blueprint id 'cal'). Its spec (.works/works.yml), shape (.works/template.yml) and documentation (README.md) live there and only there.

Upstream is calcom/cal.diy, the Open Scheduling community edition, whose own name is Cal.diy; the trademark notice refers to that name. Tags v6.2.0 and older are a different licence and code base, hence refs.exclude.

Released 2026-10-17 as status 'beta' (selectable): tag v0.1.0 (= blueprint.version) was created on main head 55de074b7feeb82ede98d2c31eedd28201ebba01, and the spec validates in blueprint mode with 0 errors. Still unverified: nothing has run on a cluster (blueprint.verified false), and the spec's blueprint.sha is still the all-zero placeholder.

template.ref is the tag v0.1.0 and template.sha its commit (55de074b7feeb82ede98d2c31eedd28201ebba01), as CONTRIBUTING.md's release step requires. Moving to 'production' needs a green verification run on a cluster.

Metadata-only, as the repository actually is (its .works/template.yml says so; it is not a fork): the template holds our metadata and no application source, so provisioning forks TWO repositories — calcom/cal.diy first (the Work Repository), then the template (provenance).
Re-creating the template as a public fork of calcom/cal.diy (code-bearing, one fork at provisioning) remains a future option; it would change this row and the template's .works/template.yml together.
The protected branding paths are part of the spec (display.protectedPaths in .works/works.yml) and are no longer copied into this row.

templates.name: Umami
templates.summary: Privacy-first, cookieless web analytics: one container, one Postgres, heartbeat health check.
notes: Template repository ever-works/umami-template. Its spec (.works/works.yml), shape (.works/template.yml) and documentation (README.md) live there and only there.

Metadata-only: the template holds our metadata and no application source. The app source stays in umami-software/umami, so provisioning forks TWO repositories (the app source first, the template second); the App Work's Work Repository is the app-source fork.

The spec deploys the upstream's published image pinned by digest, so a run spends no build minutes; switching build.strategy to dockerfile builds the fork, which is why the app-source fork must exist (template README, 'Evolving an Umami App Work').

Released 2026-10-17 as status 'beta' (selectable): tag v0.1.0 (= blueprint.version) was created on main head 7aeb58047d1796ecf7826ef5e09a513e160473ec, and the spec validates in blueprint mode with 0 errors. Still unverified: nothing has run on a cluster (blueprint.verified false), and the spec's blueprint.sha is still the all-zero placeholder.

template.ref is the tag v0.1.0 and template.sha its commit (7aeb58047d1796ecf7826ef5e09a513e160473ec), as CONTRIBUTING.md's release step requires. Moving to 'production' needs a green verification run on a cluster.

notes: E2E BRANCH ONLY (APW-13 T29, ACCEPTANCE.md §0.3): dev/stage pin EVER_WORKS_APPS_CATALOG_REF to a commit of this branch; production pins main and never lists this row.

The fixture Blueprint ever-works/app-fixture-hello-template stays PRIVATE (owner decision 2026-09-26). Since 2026-10-17 its spec is at .works/works.yml (template.yml specPath; the root app-spec.yml is a superseded copy).

Stays 'placeholder': this repository's CI token cannot read a private repository. The platform resolver does not read this listing; since 2026-10-17 it resolves a PRIVATE ever-works Blueprint for a source owned by ever-works or listed in EVER_WORKS_APPS_PRIVATE_BLUEPRINT_OWNERS, so app-fixture-hello (probe) and generated upstreams (explicit id) resolve.

Generated upstreams: <e2e-upstream-org>/app-fixture-gen-* (that is, ever-works/app-fixture-gen-<runId>) must resolve to this Blueprint (spec FR-9, ACC-13-21). The schema cannot express a glob in upstreams[].repo, so the prefix is recorded here until it can.
